note_fr: Enregistrement public de la version 1.1 du protocole d'auto-évaluation de Gardien RGPD, écrite le 26 octobre 2026 après la campagne 1.0 et publiée AVANT toute campagne 1.1. La campagne 1.1 et ses résultats doivent correspondre à ces empreintes : le protocole (docs/PROTOCOLE.md, section « Version 1.1 »), sa spécification (tools/protocol/spec.py), les outils et le paquet exécuté sur le serveur, et le plan de 1 019 385 documents (inchangé). Deux indices publiés : documents normalisés (l'indice principal, cible 95 % ou plus) et documents difficiles (équipe rouge entière). Le résultat 1.0 (61,8 % [58,6–66,9], sept familles) reste publié tel quel.
note_en: Public registration of version 1.1 of the GDPR Guardian self-rating protocol, written on 26 October 2026 after the 1.0 campaign and published BEFORE any 1.1 campaign. The 1.1 campaign and its results must match these digests: the protocol (docs/PROTOCOLE.md, 'Version 1.1' section), its specification (tools/protocol/spec.py), the tools and the bundle run on the server, and the plan of 1,019,385 documents (unchanged). Two published indexes: normalised documents (the headline, target 95% or more) and difficult documents (the whole red team). The 1.0 result (61.8% [58.6-66.9], seven families) stays published as it is.
confidence_index: normalised documents (the headline, site keys confidence_*; target 95% or more, a goal, not a guard): share of documents in which no direct identifier stays readable, 4 families equally weighted (synthetic_fr, bodacc_fr, boamp_fr, parlamint_fr), real corpora counted on their test halves only, 95% bootstrap interval stratified by family (2,000 resamples, seed 20261025)
hard_index: difficult documents (site keys hard_*): same measure over the whole red team, 51 operators in three groups (damaged everyday formats 25, deliberate obfuscations 25, OCR noise 1); every mutated document counts once (operators pooled, a group weighs its share of the documents); 95% bootstrap interval stratified by group (2,000 resamples, seed 20261025); per-group and per-operator figures published
published_apart: old press (low-quality OCR: degraded performance; outside the use case, and at 272 test documents it would weigh about 0.05% of the pooled difficult index), MAPA FR, other languages and the Judilibre control, in neither index
changes: one use case: texts organisations send to an AI (e-mails, chat requests, internal documents), in French, as text or office files, written in good faith

scope of a leak written down: any readable character of a postal address, phone, e-mail or other direct identifier whoever it belongs to, or of a natural person's name; company names counted neither as a leak nor as over-masking of neutral text (GDPR recital 14; CJEU C-92/09 and C-93/09; the published precision still counts a masked company name as an unneeded mask, as in 1.0); sole traders are persons; a town alone, or a postcode and town without street or postal box, is a place

two published indexes, each with its 95% interval, decided on 26 October 2026 before any published registration and any 1.1 campaign (they replace an unregistered single-index first draft of 5 families with the everyday red team): normalised documents (headline, target 95%+) and difficult documents
normalised index: 4 families, 1/4 each (synthetic FR, BODACC, BOAMP, ParlaMint-FR), instead of 7 families, 1/7 each; no red team in it
difficult index: all 51 red-team operators, every mutated document counting once, interval stratified by group; the 1.0 red-team family's measure, hence comparable with it

red-team groups: damaged everyday formats (25; crlf and line_break = a line break INSIDE the identifier; letter_spacing = PDF letter spacing): crlf, line_break, letter_spacing, nbsp, narrow_nbsp, thin_space, figure_space, ideographic_space, tab, double_space, dots, hyphens, slashes, compact, regroup, en_dash_groups, nb_hyphen, pdf_hyphenation, soft_hyphen, upper, lower, surname_first, strip_accents, nfd, markdown_bold; deliberate obfuscations (25): math_bold, fullwidth, superscript, arabic_indic, devanagari, cyrillic, greek, zero_width_space, zero_width_joiner, word_joiner, bom, bidi_mark, bidi_isolate, tag_chars, variation_selector, grapheme_joiner, hangul_filler, at_entity, at_percent, at_fullwidth, at_brackets, at_parens, arobase, dot_brackets, dot_point; OCR noise (1): ocr

published apart, in neither index: old press Europeana + HIPE (low-quality OCR, degraded performance); MAPA FR (EU legal texts, outside the use case, 6 scored test documents; reverses the 1.0 choice to keep it); other languages; the Judilibre control

effect on the frozen 1.0 engine, dev halves: headline 59.7% (1.0, 7 families) -> 82.8% [81.3-84.1] (normalised, 4 families); difficult 62.3% [61.8-62.9] (27,441 mutated documents); the move of the everyday red team out of the headline (+5.4 points over the first draft's 77.4%) was decided knowing it was the lowest family the first draft kept

test halves not blind: engine 1.0.1 is rated on the same test halves as 1.0 (measured at least nine times before, per-family scores published), a declared departure from section 3 (fresh data for a later engine); real-corpus figures are therefore optimistic
results written to protocol-1.1-<date>.{json,md}; run-protocol.sh finish never overwrites an existing result; the site merge refuses while the site or README still show earlier-version text

BOAMP gold aligned with the scope (tools/corpus/build_boamp.py): glued or dotted postal boxes and streets written in the postcode/town fields are addresses; services in the contact field are not persons (42 ADDRESS added, 35 LOCATION and 5 PERSON removed, 40 documents of 3,000, 18 in the test half)
test halves no longer blind: the 26 October 1.0 campaign and the 26 October rules3 evaluation added to spec.TEST_HALVES_MEASURED_BEFORE; the 1.0 campaign listed in spec.EARLIER_CAMPAIGNS

report and site merge: both indexes with their intervals and the per-group breakdown; site keys confidence_* for the normalised index (protocol_families = 4) and hard_index, hard_ci_low, hard_ci_high, hard_docs, hard_mention_recall_pct for the difficult one; red-team groups under families_apart with "index": "hard"; a 1.1 result without the difficult index is refused; the 1.0 result recalled at merge time
declared limit: the difficult index's interval resamples mutated documents one by one, not by base document, so it is too narrow

sections 8 and 12 under 1.1 (what could flatter the index, real weight): the two favourable families (synthetic, ParlaMint-FR partial gold) weigh 1/2 of the headline instead of 2/7, ParlaMint-FR alone 1/4 instead of 1/7; difficult documents leave the headline and make the second index; 3/4 of the headline rest on the scored real test-half documents of BODACC, BOAMP and ParlaMint-FR (2,886 in the 1.0 campaign); volume buys no weight in the headline only, the difficult index is pooled

unchanged: leak, readability and failure definitions, the normalised index's bootstrap stratified by family, guards, dev/test split, seeds, campaign plan and its fingerprints, tool, container, route and service options (new: the difficult index's pooled bootstrap stratified by group)

previous.note: the 1.0 digests in PROTOCOL-REGISTRATION.json match the files as they were at the 1.0 registration (repository history), not the 1.1 files; the 1.0 result copies them
